cases.sentence: На робкий ___ Пьера после прочтения письма, она отвечала просьбой, чтоб он ехал, но только определил бы ей верно время возвращения.
cases.explain: «вопросительный взгляд» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: On reading that letter (she always read her husband’s letters) Natásha herself suggested that he should go to Petersburg, though she would feel his absence very acutely. She attributed immense importance to all her husband’s intellectual and abstract interests though she did not understand them, and she always dreaded being a hindrance to him in such matters. To Pierre’s timid look of inquiry after reading the letter she replied by asking him to go, but to fix a definite date for his return. He was given four weeks’ leave of absence.

cases.sentence: Денисов, отставной, недовольный ___ генерал, приехавший в эти последние две недели, с удивлением и грустью, как на непохожий портрет когда-то любимого человека, смотрел на Наташу.
cases.explain: «настоящим положением» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Denísov, now a general on the retired list and much dissatisfied with the present state of affairs, had arrived during that fortnight. He looked at Natásha with sorrow and surprise as at a bad likeness of a person once dear. A dull, dejected look, random replies, and talk about the nursery was all he saw and heard from his former enchantress.

cases.sentence: — Всё глупости, всё пустяки, — говорила Наташа, — все его размышления, которые ни к чему не ведут, и все эти ___, — говорила она о тех самых делах, в великую важность которых она твердо верила.
cases.explain: «дурацкие общества» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “It’s all nonsense, all rubbish—those discussions which lead to nothing and all those idiotic societies!” Natásha declared of the very affairs in the immense importance of which she firmly believed.

cases.sentence: — Всё глупости, всё пустяки, — говорила Наташа, — все его размышления, которые ни к чему не ведут, и все эти дурацкие общества, — говорила она о тех ___, в великую важность которых она твердо верила.
cases.explain: «самых делах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “It’s all nonsense, all rubbish—those discussions which lead to nothing and all those idiotic societies!” Natásha declared of the very affairs in the immense importance of which she firmly believed.

cases.sentence: И она уходила в детскую кормить своего ___ Петю.
cases.explain: «единственного мальчика» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: Никто ничего не мог ей сказать столько успокоивающего, разумного, сколько это трехмесячное ___, когда оно лежало у ее груди, и она чувствовала его движение рта и сопенье носиком.
cases.explain: «маленькое существо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: And she would go to the nursery to nurse Pétya, her only boy. No one else could tell her anything so comforting or so reasonable as this little three-month-old creature when he lay at her breast and she was conscious of the movement of his lips and the snuffling of his little nose. That creature said: “You are angry, you are jealous, you would like to pay him out, you are afraid—but here am I! And I am he …” and that was unanswerable. It was more than true.

cases.sentence: — ___ спросила Наташа, боясь пошевелиться, чтобы не разбудить засыпавшего ребенка.
cases.explain: «быстрым шопотом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Has he come?” Natásha asked quickly in a whisper, afraid to move lest she should rouse the dozing baby.

cases.sentence: Потихоньку отняв грудь, Наташа покачала его, передала няне и пошла ___ в дверь.
cases.explain: «быстрыми шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Cautiously withdrawing her breast, Natásha rocked him a little, handed him to the nurse, and went with rapid steps toward the door. But at the door she stopped as if her conscience reproached her for having in her joy left the child too soon, and she glanced round. The nurse with raised elbows was lifting the infant over the rail of his cot.

cases.sentence: И вдруг она вспомнила все те муки ожидания, которые она перечувствовала в последние две недели: сияющая на ее лице радость скрылась; она нахмурилась, и поток упреков и ___ излился на Пьера.
cases.explain: «злых слов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Then all at once she remembered the tortures of suspense she had experienced for the last fortnight, and the joy that had lit up her face vanished; she frowned and overwhelmed Pierre with a torrent of reproaches and angry words.

cases.sentence: На ___ его с раскрытым беззубым ртом, остановилась веселая улыбка.
cases.explain: «широком лице» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: When Nikoláy and his wife came to look for Pierre he was in the nursery holding his baby son, who was again awake, on his huge right palm and dandling him. A blissful bright smile was fixed on the baby’s broad face with its toothless open mouth. The storm was long since over and there was bright, joyous sunshine on Natásha’s face as she gazed tenderly at her husband and child.

cases.sentence: — Не понимаю, не могу, — сказал Николай ___ глядя на ребенка.
cases.explain: «холодным взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I don’t and can’t,” replied Nikoláy, looking coldly at the baby. “A lump of flesh. Come along, Pierre!”

cases.sentence: — Ведь главное, он такой ___, — сказала графиня Марья, оправдывая своего мужа; — но только, когда уже год или этак...
cases.explain: «нежный отец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “And yet he’s such an affectionate father,” said Countess Márya, vindicating her husband, “but only after they are a year old or so …”
